messages:
Marta: Quick follow-up on the guardrail admission boundaries RFC — want to sync on tradeoffs before we fold into the deploy plan.

Chen: 👍 quick notes: central vs edge admission — central gives global fairness but is a single point; edge gives lower latency but inconsistent fairness windows.

Josh: runtime note — if we push more admission to edge, we need a lightweight repr of global shape: use a leased token bucket proto: {lease_id, weight, expiry}.

Sara: security: also need to ensure abuse signal can't be spoofed. Don't accept client-side score. Only internal signal from detector pipeline. KMS for audit logs.

Elena: ops: we need metrics for 'admissions_denied_by_policy' + 'probation_evictions' and a histogram of penalty durations.

Chen: tradeoff on fallback: can we fallback to a cheaper model variant automatically? That helps availability but complicates billing and QoS.

Marta: agreed — fallback policy should be explicit per-tenant with opt-in. Default: throttle + 503 with Retry-After header.

Josh: runtime implementation plan: add admission hook in front of request mux; small memcache for recent tenant tokens, probe latency < 1ms.

Sara: note: for regulated tenants we must allow customer-controlled private admission (Private deployments). That means an interface contract: admit(request, token) -> decision. Document it.

Marta: action items: (1) Chen + Josh to sketch the edge vs central proto + perf budget, (2) Sara to write abuse-signal attestation requirements, (3) Elena to propose observability dashboard. Sync later this week? @Chen @Josh @Sara @Elena

deploy-bot: deployment pipeline started for branch rfc/guardrail-admit (staging). :rocket:

Marta: thanks — I'll add to agenda for Friday design sync.
